input.prompt: From this Snap Inc 10-K for fiscal 2024: {{snap10k2024}}. Find the table of potentially dilutive shares excluded from diluted net loss per share as of December 31, 2024 (Stock options, Unvested RSUs and RSAs, Convertible Notes if-converted), and the conversion rates/conversion prices and maximum shares issuable on conversion for each convertible senior notes series (2025, 2026, 2027, 2028, 2030 notes). Also any statement about the maximum shares issuable under the capped calls or note conversion. Quote the exact figures and their dates.

calls.output:
## Potentially dilutive shares excluded from diluted EPS (Note 3)

The filing reports these as of each year-end, in thousands of shares:

| As of December 31 | 2024 | 2023 | 2022 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Stock options | 680 | 1,697 | 3,159 |
| Unvested RSUs and RSAs | 134,253 | 157,130 | 132,392 |
| Convertible Notes (if-converted) | 85,945 | 89,379 | 89,379 |

These were excluded because including them would have been anti-dilutive, given the net losses in each period.

## Convertible senior notes: conversion rates and prices

The filing states these terms and principal amounts as of December 31, 2024 (Note 7 and Item 7):

| Series | Conversion rate (shares per $1,000) | Conversion price | Principal at 12/31/2024 | Maturity |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2025 Notes | 46.1233 | ~$21.68 | $36,240K | May 1, 2025 |
| 2026 Notes | 43.8481 | ~$22.81 | $249,754K | Aug 1, 2026 |
| 2027 Notes | 11.2042 | ~$89.25 | $1,150,000K | May 1, 2027 |
| 2028 Notes | 17.7494 | ~$56.34 | $1,500,000K | Mar 1, 2028 |
| 2030 Notes | 45.0846 | ~$22.18 | $750,000K | May 1, 2030 |

The filing does not state a maximum share count for each series. The shares issuable below are my calculation: principal × conversion rate, using the 12/31/2024 principal.

| Series | Approx. shares issuable (thousands) |
|---|---|
| 2025 | 1,671.5 |
| 2026 | 10,951.2 |
| 2027 | 12,884.8 |
| 2028 | 26,624.1 |
| 2030 | 33,813.5 |
| **Total** | **≈85,945** |

The total matches the 85,945 thousand "Convertible Notes (if-converted)" figure reported for 2024, which suggests that figure uses the 12/31/2024 principal at the stated conversion rates. The conversion rates are subject to customary adjustments, and the 2030 Notes also carry a make-whole conversion-rate increase that the filing does not quantify.

Other conversion terms stated in the filing:
- The company may settle conversions in cash, Class A shares, or a combination, at its election.
- The sale-price condition was not met at 12/31/2024, so the 2026, 2027, 2028, and 2030 Notes are not eligible for optional conversion in Q1 2025. The 2025 Notes become convertible at any time on or after February 1, 2025, until the second scheduled trading day before maturity.
- The 2030 Notes are not eligible for optional conversion during Q1 2025.

## Capped call transactions

- The filing gives initial cap prices per Class A share of **$32.12 (2025), $32.58 (2026), $121.02 (2027), $93.90 (2028), and $33.48 (2030)**, all subject to adjustment.
- Net costs were $100.0M, $102.1M, $86.8M, $177.0M, and $68.9M, respectively.
- The capped calls are intended to reduce dilution up to the cap prices, or to offset cash payments above principal, subject to the cap.
- In May 2024 the company terminated all 2025 Capped Call Transactions for $62.7M of proceeds.
- As of December 31, 2024, the remaining capped calls were out-of-the-money.
- **The filing does not state a maximum number of shares issuable under the capped calls**, so no such figure can be quoted.

steps.text:
**Answer: about 85.95 million shares (85,945 thousand).** That is the if-converted share count for Snap's convertible senior notes as of December 31, 2024, as reported in the FY2024 10-K. Under a stricter "maximum" reading that uses the 2030 notes' maximum conversion rate, the figure would be higher, roughly 96.9 million (my calculation, explained below).

**How I got it**

1. **Reported figure.** The FY2024 10-K (filed February 5, 2025) lists potentially dilutive shares excluded from diluted net loss per share because they were anti-dilutive. As of December 31, 2024, the Convertible Notes (if-converted) line was 85,945 thousand shares. The same line was 89,379 thousand in 2023. The stock options (680 thousand) and unvested RSUs/RSAs (134,253 thousand) lines are not part of this answer. Source: Snap's FY2024 10-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1564408/000156440825000019/snap-20241231.htm). I pulled these figures through a summarizing tool, so I could not check the table cell by cell.

2. **Cross-check by series.** The filing's conversion rates and 12/31/2024 principal amounts give the following shares issuable (principal × conversion rate, in thousands):

| Series | Principal ($K) | Conversion rate (per $1,000) | Shares (K) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2025 | 36,240 | 46.1233 | 1,671.5 |
| 2026 | 249,754 | 43.8481 | 10,951.2 |
| 2027 | 1,150,000 | 11.2042 | 12,884.8 |
| 2028 | 1,500,000 | 17.7494 | 26,624.1 |
| 2030 | 750,000 | 45.0846 | 33,813.5 |
| **Total** | | | **≈85,945** |

The sum matches the reported 85,945 thousand.

3. **The 2030 notes' maximum.** Snap's May 2024 8-K says that, including the full exercise of the initial purchasers' option, a maximum of 44,802,825 Class A shares may be issued on conversion of the 2030 notes, based on a maximum conversion rate of 59.7371 shares per $1,000. That is above the base-rate figure of 33,813.5 thousand. Substituting it into the table gives 85,945.1 − 33,813.5 + 44,802.8 ≈ 96,934 thousand. I could not find maximum share counts for the other series, so this is only a partial upper bound.

**Caveats**
- The 10-K does not state a maximum share count for each series, so the 85,945 thousand figure is the if-converted number the filing reports.
- The 2030 notes also carry a make-whole conversion-rate increase, which the filing does not quantify.
- The capped call transactions reduce dilution up to their cap prices, but the filing gives no maximum share count for them, so they are not netted out here.
